function: NN design of the BS digital precoder (Tx) or digital combiner (Rx) compensating combined THz hardware impairments in hybrid beamforming, using a stage-1 DNN impairment model (pp. 6-8).
system: Point-to-point THz UM-MIMO with fully connected hybrid beamforming, Nt=Nr=256 antennas, Lt=Lr=4 RF chains, Ns=4 streams, 1 GHz bandwidth, carrier not stated; no RIS (pp. 3, 10).
method: Supervised DNN: stage 1 per-RF-chain/per-antenna sub-NNs (one tanh hidden layer) model impairments; stage 2 sub-NNs output the compensating precoder/combiner; MSE loss; pruning and parameter-sharing slimming (pp. 7-9).
data_channel: MATLAB simulation: 8000 16-QAM symbols through modelled impairments (AQNM, IQ imbalance, phase noise, phase-shifter errors, Rapp PA) for training, another 8000 for testing; channel model unspecified (pp. 10-11).
test_conditions: Fixed IQ-imbalance, PA and phase-shifter parameters; test on another 8000 symbols of the same system; retrained per transmit power (-10 to 15 dBm); uncoded and coded tests (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Uncompensated non-ideal system and ideal-hardware reference; direct DNN (D-DNN, fully connected network after [30]); Tx versus Rx compensation and slimming variants (pp. 10-12).
metrics: SER (uncoded and coded), training loss, representation approximation error, constellations, number of parameters, running time (pp. 10-13).
complexity: Parameters (Lt+Nt+Lr)(5Nh+2): 13728 unslimmed, 336-378 combined slimming (Table II); runtime 13.01 s down to 3.63 s (Table III); O(Nh(Lt+Nt+Lr)) (pp. 9, 12-13).
q1_support: p. 10: "we generate the training data through simulation"; the channel H of the system model (p. 3) is never given a model, and no 3GPP, COST 2100, ray-tracing or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 11: "the neural network needs to be retrained at different transmit power"; the test set is "another 8000 transmit symbols" (p. 10) of the same simulated system, a held-out split, not a new condition.
q3_support: p. 11: "we also compared the proposed methods with the direct-DNN (D-DNN) approach [30]"; p. 12: "We compare the performance of the ideal system, non-ideal system, non-ideal system with combined slimming methods, and non-ideal system with D-DNN." Both on SER.
q4_support: p. 13: "the computational complexity of these two combined methods is O(Nh (Lt + Nt + Lr)) and O(Nh (Lt + Lr))"; parameter counts in Table II (p. 12) and running times in Table III (p. 13).
q5_support: p. 11: "the generation of the training and testing data are operated in Matlab"; the data are simulated and the paper gives no code or data link.
notes: PDF is arXiv 2411.14699v1; its title and authors match the DOI record. Area 3 because the learned output is the digital precoder of the BS hybrid beamformer (p. 8; 'all nonlinear PAs in BS', p. 9), and the paper prefers Tx compensation (p. 11); the Rx-combiner variant and the SER metric could argue for area 1, reviewer to confirm. Eligibility: the function borders on hardware-impairment compensation/predistortion (amplifier linearization is an excluded function), but it covers quantization, IQ imbalance, phase noise and phase-shifter errors at Tx and Rx, not only the PA, and outputs a MIMO precoder or combiner, so I included it; reviewer to confirm. q3: the non-learned baseline is the uncompensated system ('With all errors' in Figs. 7(c), 9, 10), a simple no-compensation baseline analogous to a fixed RIS configuration; the learned baseline is D-DNN, a fully connected network from the earlier work [30]. q2: the coded-system test (p. 12) keeps the same impairments and 16-QAM symbols and the paper does not present it as a new condition, so not counted.
